title: Trade-Off: Which Problem Do I Want?
coreMove: Name the cost inside each option and choose the burden attached to the more essential contribution.
sourcePressure: The chapter insists that trade-offs are real and that the essentialist stops asking how to do both and starts choosing which problem is worth carrying.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: A weak run would frame trade-offs as temporary obstacles that clever scheduling can overcome.

hook: generic trade-off: which problem do i want? topic opener
tryThisNow: set a timer for ninety seconds...
make a list of priorities without a trade-off
generic say no to one thing today

exampleSpecs.domain: coastal town deciding between dune restoration and expanded parking before tourist season
exampleSpecs.audience: town planner facing two politically defensible choices
exampleSpecs.stakes: either choice creates a real problem someone must own
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: She places the flood model beside the parking revenue sheet and asks which problem the council chooses to carry.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A flood model sits beside a parking revenue sheet.

exampleSpecs.domain: documentary editor choosing between a festival deadline and verifying a disputed interview
exampleSpecs.audience: editor pulled between prestige and accuracy
exampleSpecs.stakes: speed can gain a premiere while risking trust
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: He freezes the timeline on the disputed quote and writes the cost under festival yes and verification yes.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A paused timeline frame shows a disputed interview.

exampleSpecs.domain: regional seed farmer choosing between a high-yield hybrid contract and preserving a rare local variety
exampleSpecs.stakes: one season’s profit can crowd out the seed stock that makes future resilience possible
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: She weighs the contract packet against the rare-seed envelopes and names which problem she can sleep with.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Rare-seed envelopes sit under a contract packet.

exampleSpecs.domain: fire department captain assigning one engine during simultaneous calls
exampleSpecs.stakes: pretending both calls get equal response hides the burden
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: He taps the dispatch board and chooses the engine assignment while naming the unserved risk out loud.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A dispatch board flashes two red call cards.

exampleSpecs.domain: graduate pianist choosing between a competition circuit and months of injury rehabilitation
exampleSpecs.audience: musician choosing between career exposure and long-term capacity
exampleSpecs.stakes: avoiding the trade-off risks losing both performance and hand health
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Before, she keeps both calendars; after, she writes the pain score beside each audition date and withdraws from two.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A pain-score notebook lies across audition dates.

exampleSpecs.domain: city newspaper deciding whether to keep the court reporter or launch a lifestyle newsletter
exampleSpecs.audience: publisher choosing mission risk versus revenue experiment
exampleSpecs.stakes: the paper cannot staff both without thinning public accountability
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: The publisher reviews the empty courthouse notebook after a missed ruling and names the cost of chasing newsletter growth.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: An empty courthouse notebook rests beside a newsletter mockup.

skillTargets: identify the Trade-Off: Which Problem Do I Want? move inside a concrete scenario
choose the response that applies: Name the cost inside each option and choose the burden attached to the more essential contribution.
reject the generic drift: A weak run would frame trade-offs as temporary obstacles that clever scheduling can overcome.
explain the trade-off using chapter-specific terms rather than generic productivity language

tryThisNowSpec: Choose one decision where you keep asking how to do both. Write the cost under each yes, then circle the burden you are willing to carry.
